name: Notion
one_liner: Workspace of pages and databases with a public REST API at api.notion.com.
auth_notes: Personal access tokens (self-created in Developer portal) and internal/public connection tokens as Bearer; OAuth 2.0 authorization code for public connections. Pages must be shared with the connection. On Business/Enterprise, PAT creation is restricted by default until a workspace owner enables it.
access_notes: Quickstart needs only a Notion account and a PAT from the Developer portal; no plan tier required. Business/Enterprise admins may restrict PAT creation.
sandbox_or_test_env: Use a free personal workspace (no dedicated sandbox documented)

buildability.rationale: Self-serve PAT and OAuth, documented REST with webhooks and rate limits (180 or 600 req/min per connection). Per-page sharing with the connection is a usage caveat, not an access gate.

disputes.why: Quickstart: need only a Notion account and terminal; PAT created self-serve in Developer portal.
Request limits page gives 180 or 600 requests per minute per connection by plan.
Page-sharing is normal scope behavior of the connection model, not a blocker; credentials self-serve, standard auth.

auth.quote: A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.

access.quote: You need a Notion account and a terminal.
On Business and Enterprise plans, PAT creation is restricted by default. Ask a workspace owner to enable it

sandbox.quote: Workspace plan limits are separate from request limits.

api_surface.quote: | Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second) |
Whenever a page or database changes, Notion sends a secure HTTP POST request to your webhook endpoint.

mcp.quote: Notion MCP lets your AI assistant search your workspace, create and edit pages, and manage databases.

buildability.quote: | All other plans | 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second) |

identity.quote: Create a page in your Notion workspace with a personal access token and a single API request.
